# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde sits regularly at her kitchen window keeping an eye on the main road in Avonlea. She prefers strong color and snap in a girl's appearance rather than pale, big-eyed looks.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel is a capable, hardworking woman who prides herself on always speaking her mind without fear or favor. She dearly loves to be asked for advice and considers herself willing to admit when she has made a mistake. Highly outspoken and critical, she can be a meddlesome gossip who picks faults in others and nags them to do right. Despite her sharp tongue, she is a kind, good Christian woman who never shirks her share of work. She is also a passionate Liberal politician.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c15 P89](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0089), [v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v1 c18 P41](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0041), [v1 c27 P3](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow near the main road of Avonlea, keeping a close eye on all happenings in the community. She managed her house, ran the local Sewing Circle, helped run the Sunday school, and served as a strong leader in the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. When Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert decided to adopt an orphan boy, Rachel visited Green Gables out of curiosity. Later, upon meeting Anne Shirley, Rachel bluntness about Anne's looks provoked an angry outburst from the child. Though outraged at the insult, Rachel maintained her neighborly ties with Marilla and offered counsel on child-rearing. She also advised Marilla when Anne ran into trouble with schoolmaster Mr. Phillips. As an ardent Liberal, she attended a political rally in Charlottetown even though the speaking Premier was a Conservative. Over the years, Rachel admitted she had been mistaken about Anne, praising her dramatic improvement and achievements despite her continued disapproval of higher education for women.

## Quotes

> Well, they didn’t pick you for your looks, that’s sure and certain.  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say.  <sub>[v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014)</sub>

> Well, I see that I’ll have to be very careful what I say after this, Marilla, since the fine feelings of orphans, brought from goodness knows where, have to be considered before anything else. Oh, no, I’m not vexed—don’t worry yourself. I’m too sorry for you to leave any room for anger in my mind. You’ll have your own troubles with that child. But if you’ll take my advice—which I suppose you won’t do, although I’ve brought up ten children and buried two—you’ll do that ‘talking to’ you mention with a fair-sized birch switch. I should think that would be the most effective language for that kind of a child. Her temper matches her hair I guess. Well, good evening, Marilla. I hope you’ll come down to see me often as usual. But you can’t expect me to visit here again in a hurry, if I’m liable to be flown at and insulted in such a fashion. It’s something new in my experience.  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030)</sub>

> Well, since you’ve asked my advice, Marilla... I’d just humor her a little at first, that’s what I’d do. It’s my belief that Mr. Phillips was in the wrong. Of course, it doesn’t do to say so to the children, you know. And of course he did right to punish her yesterday for giving way to temper. But today it was different. The others who were late should have been punished as well as Anne, that’s what. And I don’t believe in making the girls sit with the boys for punishment. It isn’t modest. Tillie Boulter was real indignant. She took Anne’s part right through and said all the scholars did too. Anne seems real popular among them, somehow. I never thought she’d take with them so well.  <sub>[v1 c15 P89](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0089)</sub>

> I never would have thought she’d have turned out so well that first day I was here three years ago... Lawful heart, shall I ever forget that tantrum of hers! When I went home that night I says to Thomas, says I, ‘Mark my words, Thomas, Marilla Cuthbert ‘ll live to rue the step she’s took.’ But I was mistaken and I’m real glad of it. I ain’t one of those kind of people, Marilla, as can never be brought to own up that they’ve made a mistake. No, that never was my way, thank goodness. I did make a mistake in judging Anne, but it weren’t no wonder, for an odder, unexpecteder witch of a child there never was in this world, that’s what. There was no ciphering her out by the rules that worked with other children. It’s nothing short of wonderful how she’s improved these three years, but especially in looks. She’s a real pretty girl got to be, though I can’t say I’m overly partial to that pale, big-eyed style myself. I like more snap and color, like Diana Barry has or Ruby Gillis. Ruby Gillis’s looks are real showy. But somehow—I don’t know how it is but when Anne and them are together, though she ain’t half as handsome, she makes them look kind of common and overdone—something like them white June lilies she calls narcissus alongside of the big, red peonies, that’s what.  <sub>[v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043)</sub>
